mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.0% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the following 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative despite the FEDFUNDS increase, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression controlling for GDP growth and yield curve slope.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points within the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative despite the labor indicators moving in the predicted direction, or the interaction term is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.2% growth for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand, which elevates earnings expectations and drives S&P 500 forward returns positive in the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day cumulative forward return is negative when the consumption momentum persists, or the effect is not captured in a Granger causality test (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in the ratio of orders to shipments (not directly observable here but implied by INDPRO trend) suggests supply-side constraints, which can lead to S&P 500 forward returns turning negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the supply contraction, or the correlation with INDPRO is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the discount rate applied to future earnings is expected to rise, reducing the present value of expected SPX returns and producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or neutral when the policy rate condition is met, or the effect is not robust to out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a wage-price spiral, raising labor costs for firms and reducing profit margins, which in turn drags S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 3.5% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the low-unemployment period, or the wage-price effect is not identified in a difference-in-differences setup.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of accelerating retail sales growth (implied by HOUST) exceeding 2% suggests consumer optimism that persists into the near term, elevating equity valuations and generating positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the retail sales acceleration, or the signal is not predictive in a rolling window regression.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over three consecutive months, especially when accompanied by rising inflation (CPIAUCSL), indicates a supply-side contraction that weighs on corporate earnings expectations and produces negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months while CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.3% in the same period
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive despite the combined indicators moving in the predicted direction, or the interaction is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
